correctness.rationale: For real SPD A, exact nonterminal Lanczos with H=V^TAV strictly irreducible SPD tridiagonal and beta>0, Gaussian sketch regression g=(Z^TZ)^(-1) Z^T w has multivariate Student density f_{k,ell}(g)=Gamma((ell+1)/2)/(pi^(k/2)Gamma((ell-k+1)/2))*(1+||g||²)^(-(ell+1)/2), nu=ell-k+1. Sketched Galerkin projected equation (H+beta g e_k^T)y_F=||b||e_1 leads by Sherman–Morrison to y_F=y0-c H^-1g/(1+a^Tg), a=beta H^-1e_k, c=beta||b||e_k^T H^-1e1!=0 by the off-corner cofactor of irreducible tridiagonal H. Energy orthogonality yields squared error D²+c² g^T H^-1g/(1+a^Tg)². Its strictly positive numerator along the entire affine hyperplane a^Tg=-1 causes exactly p>=1 divergent moments regardless of ell and gives a positive 1/R tail with the stated coarea integral; local transversal integration and Student radial domination prove p<1 convergence and finite tail coefficient. For sketched least squares, independent Gaussian orthogonal regression about nonzero deterministic residual yields an invertible linear image of a multivariate Student vector, giving moment cutoff p<ell-k+1 including divergence at equality. Independently verified 120 random projected systems and the exact algebraic Sherman–Morrison relationship; a separate k=ell=1 Cauchy example confirmed the hyperplane tail coefficient. All asymptotic/integrability claims depend on analytic density proofs, not Monte Carlo.
